collection_summary: This instance is exhaustive relative to the cited Wikipedia accession chronology and cited capital list. It joins the accession cohorts enumerated on the 'Enlargement of NATO' Wikipedia page (1999-2024 range) with capital-city values from the 'List of national capitals' Wikipedia page. The sources are Tier B (manual_wikipedia), not official NATO or government datasets; exhaustiveness is relative to what those two pages enumerate, not to any external authoritative register.
source_coverage_notes: The enlargement page explicitly enumerates the relevant accession groups: Czech Republic, Hungary, and Poland in 1999; Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia in 2004; Albania and Croatia in 2009; Montenegro in 2017; North Macedonia in 2020; Finland in 2023; and Sweden in 2024. The capital list supplies one capital-city value for each of those countries. Together the two pages support a 16-row joined table for the 1999-2024 range.
decision_log: Chose a multi-source historical join as the next forward test of the curation skill after the single-source eurozone instance. Set the primary category to implicit_join because the benchmark-relevant work is combining accession chronology with capital-city lookup, while recording temporal as the secondary category because the year-range filter is still important. Marked the claim type as exhaustive because the accession source is an explicit historical list rather than a source-defined subset.
normalization_decisions: Country names follow the English names on the enlargement page. Accession years are stored as bare integers. Capital cities use the conventional English names from the national-capitals list and are typed as 'categorical' (consistent controlled labels) rather than 'text' (free-form strings) — corrected during prepare-registration review. The primary key is Country because each accessioning country appears once in the filtered historical slice.
open_questions: If later benchmark policy wants stronger non-Wikipedia sourcing for political-history joins, this instance could be rebuilt by replacing the accession page with the official NATO member-country chronology and replacing the capitals source with a non-Wikipedia country-capitals dataset. The current staged version is still valid under the manual_wikipedia tier.
